  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]

  WHY: The failure path assigns a local `false` value but only the success path exports the final state, so later prompt-building can see stale Serena availability.

  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]

  WHY: The gate is broader than the actual dependency, so Serena-only runs waste runner time setting up uv with no benefit.

  WHY: The old code constructed `DIAGNOSE_SERENA_TOOL_HINTS` when `SERENA_AVAILABLE=true` and passed it via `SERENA_TOOL_HINTS=... bash scripts/render_prompt.sh ...`; removing that logic drops Serena guidance from the prompt.
- prompts/mode-validate-fix-harness.txt:3 | confidence=4

  WHY: The fix-harness prompt is passed directly, so the LLM will see the literal placeholder text instead of rendered Serena guidance.
- scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh:105-109 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The `sed -i` replacement for `model_reasoning_effort` is guarded by `|| true`, which silently masks any sed failure.
  WHY: If sed fails, `~/.codex/config.toml` may be left with an incorrect or missing `model_reasoning_effort` key while the function still returns success.
- scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh:105-112 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The new `grep -Eq` + `sed` approach matches and rewrites `model_reasoning_effort` anywhere in the file, including inside TOML table sections.
  WHY: The removed Python logic only rewrote the top-level section before the first TOML table header, so this version can silently corrupt section-specific values.
